title: Single tetrahedron, format 2.2
why: Smallest possible solid. Volume = 1/6 from the formula base x height / 3.

title: Single tetrahedron, format 4.1, node numbers 10, 20, 30, 40
why: Node numbers in files needn't be consecutive. A reader that assumes they are gets a wrong mesh.

title: unit square 2d
why: 2D unit square with four named sides. Area and each side length are 1.

title: unit square at z5
why: The same square at height z = 5. A flat mesh needn't sit at z = 0.

title: unit square crlf
why: The same square saved with Windows line endings.

title: Two tetrahedra sharing a face, with tags
why: Volume = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2. The shared face is inside, so only 6 faces make up the outer boundary.

title: Two materials with a tagged interface
why: An inner face may be tagged, for example as the boundary between steel and copper. It must not be called an error.

title: Tag names with spaces and an accent
why: Real projects use names like 'cold wall'. Names must arrive unchanged.

title: Tag name saved in an older text encoding
why: Older tools on Windows may save accents as Latin-1, not UTF-8. This must not be mistaken for a binary file.

title: One name used in two dimensions
why: Gmsh identifies a group by (dimension, number), so one name can label a curve and a surface. Asking for the surface must find the surface.

title: One tag number used in two dimensions
why: Number 1 is both a surface and a solid here, which is valid because the dimension is part of the key.

title: A named single point
why: Points can be named too, for example to fix one corner. A point has no size, but it must not be reported as empty.

title: octahedron ascii
why: Eight-sided closed solid. Volume = 4/3, area = 4 sqrt(3). STL stores separate copies of corners, which must be joined.

title: Cube with sides of 10
why: Volume = 1000, area = 600.

title: Only line cells
why: Not a solid or surface, so most checks can't apply. Reports must list them as skipped and must not invent a volume.

title: Points listed out of order
why: Files may list points in any order. Reading by position instead of by number would scramble the shape. The right answer is the same as VAL-06: volume 1/2.

title: Cylinder from real Gmsh, v22
why: Radius 1, height 4. Inlet area = pi, wall area = 8 pi, volume = 4 pi, within the faceting tolerance.

title: Cylinder from real Gmsh, v41
why: Radius 1, height 4. Inlet area = pi, wall area = 8 pi, volume = 4 pi, within the faceting tolerance.

title: Plate with a round hole
why: 2D area = 1 - pi x 0.2^2 = 0.8743. The hole is a second boundary, and it must not be reported as a defect.

title: Two joined blocks of different material
why: Two unit cubes side by side. Each volume = 1, interface = 1, outside = 10. These are flat-sided, so the match must be exact.

title: Sphere surface exported by Gmsh as STL
why: Radius 1: volume = 4/3 pi, area = 4 pi. Tests corner joining on a real export of over a thousand triangles.

title: Gmsh mesh saved without any physical groups
why: A common beginner mistake. The geometry is fine, but no region has a name, so a solver can't apply boundary conditions.

title: Checking a subset of tags and allowing others
why: A user may only care about one tag. With extra tags allowed, the others must not even be mentioned.

title: Checking a subset of tags with others not allowed
why: By default, tags you didn't list are mentioned as information. This isn't a problem, so the status stays clean.

title: Name of the wall removed
why: The cells still have a number, but the name 'wall' is gone, so a solver looking for 'wall' finds nothing.

title: Inlet renamed to 'inlett'
why: A typo gets past most workflows silently.

title: All names lost
why: A typical converter failure: numbers survive and every name is lost.

title: Wall name kept, its cells lost
why: The name still exists, so a simple name check would pass. The cells are gone.

title: All boundary cells lost
why: Only solid cells remain, and the boundary has no labels at all.

title: Half of the solid cells have no region
why: A solver assigning materials by tag would leave these cells without one.

title: Inlet labelled as a curve instead of a surface
why: The name exists, but in the wrong dimension, so a surface lookup fails.

title: Boundary triangle attached to nothing
why: Its boundary condition would act on nothing.

title: Inlet and wall swapped
why: All names exist, so only comparing sizes can reveal this: the 'inlet' measures 8 pi instead of pi.

title: The same swap, with no sizes given
why: Shows why stating sizes matters. Without them, this swap can't be detected, and the tool must not claim otherwise.

title: Inside-out tetrahedron
why: Swapping two corners makes the volume -1/6. Its total must be marked as untrusted.

title: Tetrahedron with all corners in one plane
why: Zero volume. FEM divides by cell size, so this could produce infinities.

title: Tetrahedron using one corner twice
why: Only three distinct corners, so it has no volume. The fourth point is then unused, which is noted too.

title: Extremely flat tetrahedron
why: Valid but nearly flat: height 0.0001, volume 0.0001/6. A warning, since it isn't strictly broken.

title: The same cell listed twice
why: A solver would count its stiffness twice. Volume reads 1/3 instead of 1/6.

title: Crack from a duplicated point
why: Two cells look joined, but use separate copies of one corner, so heat can't flow across.

title: Point used by no cell
why: Usually harmless, so it's only information, and the status stays clean.

title: Two separate pieces
why: A floating piece needs its own boundary conditions, or the problem can't be solved.

title: One face shared by three tetrahedra
why: A face can only have two sides, so these cells must overlap.

title: 2D mesh with one triangle flipped
why: A mesh entirely clockwise is fine, as it's merely viewed from behind. A mix isn't.

title: File with points but no cells
why: Nothing can be checked, so 'no problems found' would be seriously misleading.

title: Cube with one side missing
why: Area = 600 - 100 = 500. Its 'volume' depends on where the mesh sits, so it must be untrusted.

why: Every edge still has two triangles, so it passes a simple watertight test, yet the volume is wrong.

title: Cube turned inside out
why: All faces point inward, so volume = -1000.

title: Cube with an extra fin
why: An edge touched by three triangles has no clear inside. The fin's own edges are also open. Area = 600 + 35.355.

title: Two separate cubes
why: Volume = 2000, area = 1200. Volume is valid, but two pieces are worth a warning.

title: Text STL with no closing line
why: A file cut off between triangles could look complete, so the reader must say something's off.

why: Expected 7, measured 10. No common unit gives this ratio.

title: Just inside the tolerance
why: Expected 594.1, measured 600: a difference of 0.993% with a 1% limit.

title: Just outside the tolerance
why: Expected 590, measured 600: a difference of 1.69% with a 1% limit.

title: Loose tolerance accepts the same value
why: The same 1.69% difference with a 2% limit passes.

title: Expected volume of zero
why: A zero expectation mustn't cause a division by zero.

title: Asking an STL file for a tag
why: STL has no tags, so an expected one must be reported as missing.

title: Hexahedra only
why: Hexahedra aren't analysed. The report must say so, not imply that the mesh passed.

title: Tetrahedron plus hexahedron
why: Only the tetrahedron is counted, so the volume is too low and must be marked untrusted. The hexahedron's corners look unused.

title: Second-order Gmsh mesh
why: Curved elements aren't analysed, and the report must say so.

title: Inlet and outlet swapped, same size
why: KNOWN GAP: equal sizes can't separate them, so this goes undetected, as documented in the README.

title: Flat 2D mesh not in the xy plane
why: KNOWN GAP: only meshes of constant z are recognised as 2D. This reads as an open surface.
